details: This package is a controlled ingestion-baseline / proof-of-concept record rather than malware. It ships package/backend-canary.js, which reads /etc/hostname and the OS username, SHA-256 hashes both values, and issues an HTTPS GET to a webhook[.]site callback with the hashes in host= and user= query parameters. Only those two hashed host-metadata values are transmitted; no credentials, tokens, environment values, file contents or wallet data are collected. package.json declares no lifecycle scripts and index.js only exports a constant, so the beacon runs only when backend-canary.js is executed directly, not on install or require. This package is a controlled canary/test artifact that beacons host metadata when its module is required. package/backend-canary.js builds a request to hxxps://webhook[.]site/314c4c8c-4eba-4012-9bf5-0a45805cd355/npm-backend-574b7ccdaeb61dd9dd70d6d4/lifecycle and appends two query parameters: 'host' = sha256 of the contents of /etc/hostname and 'user' = sha256 of os.userInfo().username. The request is issued via https.get with errors swallowed. No environment variables, credential files, tokens, wallet data or file contents are read or transmitted, and no remote code is fetched or executed. The package self-declares as a controlled test artifact: package.json describes it as a "controlled... duplicate_exact_manifest" build, package/marker.txt holds the marker NPM_BACKEND_DUPLICATE_EXACT_MANIFEST_dcf4b02c31d1b1adff649d5b3b8d7818, index.js only exports the string 'controlled', and the beacon file is named backend-canary.js. Callback endpoint: hxxps://webhook[.]site/314c4c8c-4eba-4012-9bf5-0a45805cd355/npm-backend-574b7ccdaeb61dd9dd70d6d4/lifecycle.
